title: How a silent e changes a word
examples: Why is there an e at the end of cake?

figure.name: x-word
figure.note: The e is silent but makes the a say its name

explain.say: Look at the word on the board. It says cap. A cap is a hat. Listen to the middle sound. It is a short a, as in apple. Say it with me: c, a, p.

draw.text: How a silent e changes a word

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: A short a, as in apple

explain.say: Now look. One letter is added at the end. It is the letter e. You do not say this e. It makes the a say its name, ay. So cap becomes cape.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: The e is silent but makes the a say its name

explain.say: Look at the a now. It is the letter that changed its sound. A long vowel says its own name. The letter a says ay. The letter i says eye. The letter o says oh. Say cap, then cape. Listen to the change.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: The e is silent but makes the a say its name

explain.say: This works with other vowels too. Look at kite on the board. Without the e, the word is kit. With the e, the i says its name, eye. Now you try: hop and hope, cub and cube.

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: The silent e makes the i say eye

explain.say: Look at the board. Each short word on the left has a partner on the right. The partner has an e at the end. Try this. Add an e to the word not. You get note.

faq.q: What does a silent e do?
faq.a: A silent e at the end of a word is not spoken, but it makes the vowel before it say its name. Cap becomes cape and kit becomes kite.
asks: Why is there an e at the end of cake?

faq.q: What is a long vowel sound?
faq.a: A long vowel says the name of the letter: a in cake, e in Pete, i in bike, o in rope and u in cube.
In cape, the a and the e work together to make one sound, ay, with the p in between. Teachers call that a split digraph.

faq.q: Does a silent e always make the vowel long?
faq.a: Not always. In have, give and love the vowel stays short. These common words are learned by sight.
asks: Why is give not said like five?

faq.q: Was the silent e ever said out loud?
faq.a: Yes. About 600 years ago that final e was spoken. People stopped saying it, but the spelling stayed and became a handy signal for a long vowel.
asks: Why did English keep the silent e?

facts: In Chaucer's English, about 600 years ago, the final e in words like name was spoken.
Adding a silent e can make a new word: hop and hope, cut and cute, pin and pine.

quiz.say: Add a silent e to the end of tub. What new word do you get?
quiz.why: The e makes the u say its name. So tub becomes tube.

wrong.1: tubby adds the letters b and y. Here you add an e.
wrong.2: tab has a new vowel. Here you add an e to the end.

quiz.say: Look at the 3 words. Which word has an i that says its name, eye?
quiz.show: Which word has a long i?
quiz.why: In bike, the e at the end makes the i say eye.

wrong.0: bit has a short i, as in in.
wrong.2: give ends in e, but its i stays short. It is a word to learn by sight.
